Only the confirmed events are drawn; the affair and espionage allegations and the private individuals involved are left out of the picture. stories.name: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
facts: On Thursday, Nov. 12, Nvidia announced that co-founder Jensen Huang had stepped down as CEO and from its board, effective immediately, after 33 years leading the chipmaker.
CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO while keeping her finance role; Harvey C. Jones became the board's first-ever chair. The board will consider internal and external candidates.
The exit followed days of reports about Huang's personal relationships and related national security questions, which Nvidia said it was investigating; Huang made no public statement reported.
Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% early Thursday, then recovered to close down about 4.3%.

Not drawn as a figure: no public appearance was reported. Represented only by an empty, spotlit stage and his widely documented signature black leather jacket left on a stool.

stories.visual_notes: An empty keynote stage seen from low in the dark audience: a single spotlight falls on an empty stool with a black leather jacket draped over it (illustrative symbolism for the departed CEO). Behind, a giant glowing green graphics chip on the stage screen radiates circuit traces like a sunrise; across it, a red share-price line plunges steeply and recovers part of the way (the 14% intraday fall and ~4% close), with no numbers or logos. Foreground: rows of empty seat backs. No people, no text, no allegations depicted.
stories.confidence: high: AP (via NBC Boston), CBS News and CNBC, all read in full, agree on the resignation, the interim CEO, the new chair and the share-price moves. The allegations are attributed and disputed, so none are drawn or stated as fact.
